title.narrative: Reproductive Health Services Training and Education Program 2017-2021
Reproductive Health Services Training and Education Program 2017-2021

description.narrative:
Insatsen syftar på att förbättra sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa i Bangladesh och är direkt kopplad till rättighets- och fattigdomsperspektivet. Insatsen ligger också i linje med de prioriteringarna i den svenska resultatstrategin med Bangladesh och inkluderar de fyra principerna om deltagande, icke-diskriminering, öppenhet och ansvarsutkrävande på ett tillfredsställande sätt.
Ambassaden bedömer att insatsen är relevant för svenskt stöd då det inkluderar mänskliga rättigheter och jämställdhet mellan kvinnor och män som är de tematiska prioriteringar för svenskt utvecklingssamarbete. De identifierade indikatorerna bedöms vara realistiska och mätbara. Utbredd korruption, utmaningar kring projektets hållbarhet genom avsaknad av potentiella givare och växande religiösa känslor bedöms som de stora riskerna med programmet.
Som riskreducerande åtgärder måste RHSTEP ta itu med de rekommendationer som identifierats i analysen om kapacitetsbedömning, bl. a. för att minimera de interna riskerna i samband med programmet. För att minska den externa risken kommer RHSTEP att ytterligare förbättra relationen med ministeriet, gemenskapen och andra relevanta intressenter. Dessa kommer att följas upp genom dialog. Programmet kommer att kontinuerligt följas upp av ambassaden. Utfasningen av stödet till RHSTEP från Sverige sker under angiven tidsperiod. Utvärderings sker mid-term.

The purpose of the project is to contribute in reduction of Maternal Mortality, morbidity from unsafe abortion and improve the Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) situation of women and adolescents in the Project areas.
This project targets to achieve 152825 MR conducted , 38910 patient managed for Complications of unsafe abortion , distribution of 367716 FP methods , 155986 individual received Reproductive Health service at school, community and garments, Institutionalized and sustainable attention at the national level to ensure access to safe abortion and family planning.
This will be achieved by ensuring that poor and marginalized women and adolescents don't face any financial barrier to access safe MR and modern Family Planning (FP) methods; Providing comprehensive MR and PAC training to health service providers, raising awareness and creation of Demand of SRHR and Supporting Changes in the policy environments for abortion services. SRHR project will help Bangladesh to achieve universal health coverage (SDG 3), by ensuring safe MR services, increasing family planning use and reducing maternal mortality in Bangladesh and creating enabling Environment to exercise sexual reproductive Health and rights.

The overall objective of the project is to contribute in reduction of Maternal Mortality, morbidity from unsafe abortion and improve the SRHR situation of women and adolescents in the project areas. There are 7 outcomes described in the Project. Outcome-1: Improved Skills of Service providers for SRHR services.; Outcome-2: Improved capacity of the consortium in SRHR program management.. Outcome-3: Increased access to quality SRHR services for women, adolescents and men; Outcome-4: Enhanced knowledge of the women and adolescents in the project areas to make informed choice pertaining to their sexual and reproductive health needs; Outcome-5: Strengthened monitoring, Research, Evaluation and Documentation processes in the consortium. Outcome-6: Strengthened advocacy and social networking initiatives for improving SRHR situation. Outcome-7: Sustainability of the consortium improved. During the entire project period it aims to achieve 152825 MR conducted , 38910 patient managed for complications of unsafe abortion , distribution of 367716 FP methods , 155986 individual received reproductive health education and service at school, community and garments, Institutionalized and sustainable attention at the national level to ensure access to safe abortion and family planning.

title.narrative: Decision on amendment of Reproductive Health Services Training and Education Program 2017-2021

description.narrative:
This is the last annual report of the project. In reality it is a report of 14 months activities.
One of the major objectives of this project is to ensure quality SRH service provision to improve overall SRHR situation and reduction of maternal mortality. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) aim to reduce the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) to less than 70 per 100?000 live One of many preconditions of rendering such service is, forming skilled service providers.
To safeguard peoples sexual and reproductive health, the consortium has continued to impart comprehensive menstrual regulation (MR) training to the service providers of public and private sectors. Design of the comprehensive training is guided by the SRHR components which includes discussion of safe menstrual regulation services (MR), post abortion care (PAC), FP counselling, general counselling, adolescent reproductive health and so on.
To achieve the goal consortium provides comprehensive MR, MRM and PAC training to doctors, nurses, FWVs, paramedics, SACMOs and midwives. The service providers also receive necessary knowledge on gender and human rights-based approaches to incorporate that in their day-to-day practices. In this reporting period, the consortium has imparted MR, MRM and PAC training to 73 service providers which is (112%) of the planned target.
34 participants received training on Gender Based Violence & Human Resources and Future Project planning. A workshop on Prevention of Corruption and Financial Irregularities were conducted where 37 staffs of RHSTEP and BAPSA. Around 30 staffs were trained on Gender Transformative and & Human Rights Based Approach. 3 training sessions were conducted on Sexual Harassment.
During this reporting period, the consortium has rendered 791,284 (127%) services among 321,850 clients. RHSTEP served 287098 clients with 717969 (139%) services and BAPSA served 34752 clients with 73,315 (70%) services respectively. During the reporting year, 18537 (91%) clients were counselled for MR procedure and total MR related services were rendered to 18281 clients which is 91% of the target. RHSTEP rendered 15,416 (93%) and BAPSA rendered 2865 (80%) services by the trained service providers of consortium.
The consortium continued to provide short acting, long acting and permanent method support. During this reporting period, 55009 (109%) family planning services were provided to the men and women at reproductive age. Total 46003 (128%) clients were supported from RHSTEP, and 9006 (62%) clients were supported from BAPSA centres. Among all the contraceptive acceptors, non-MR contraceptive acceptors were more in number which is 22967 (105%) and number of post MR contraceptive acceptors was 16700 (105%) due to proper counselling.
Safe motherhood service is a priority more than ever. Safe motherhood services including antenatal care, delivery service and post-natal care services were provided to 32225 (107%) women in the year of the project. RHSTEP served 22262 (133%) clients during this period and BAPSA supported 9963 (74%) clients respectively. About 222(123%) normal vaginal delivery was conducted by the consortium. Nearly 1016 (76%) of the delivery cases required caesarean sectionwhich is quiet alarming . In this project year, the consortium has rendered 17836 (99%) reproductive organ cancer diagnostic and counselling service to the clients in catchment areas.
For early detection of cancer of cervix, 4947 (94%) Pap smear and VIA test was performed along with 2477 (87%) follow-up. On the other hand, for early detection of breast cancer 4648 (78%) bimanual breast cancer screening tests were performed. LCC services also includes pathology and diagnostic services among the clients in the service areas. Total 613631 (140%) LCC, pathology and diagnostic services were rendered during the reporting period among which, RHSTEP provided 577474 (147%) services and BAPSA performed 32546 (81%) services. Total, 498702 pathology and diagnostic support was provided to the clients.
Total 34455(78%) LCC service was delivered to the clients at centers and in school, community and garments 5022 services were provided accordingly. During this reporting period, 2150 clients were supported through telemedicine service from the consortium. Male were counseled while visiting consortium clinics as a clients individually or attendants of clients for LCC, RTI /STI as partners and contraceptive services. The consortium partners rendered 1870 (133%) services to male at their catchments areas in this reporting period. Alordhara Pathshala is the youth hub of RHSTEP that was working during the project period. Currently, RHSTEP is actively running 04 Pathshala centers in four distinctive areas of the country.
Alordhara Pathshala centers are mobilizing local youth and adolescents through different initiatives along with promoting SRHR knowledge and book reading. Youth and adolescents are the group that largely adopted a modification in their life style during this times. Due to less sharing attitude with parents & guardian but more with peer, psychological burden is an increasing trend among this group of people. Alordhara Pathshala played an integral part in mobilizing the local youth and adolescents during this time to support them psychologically.
The door of Pathshala was open to the youth to circulate books, disseminate information through fun activities and so on. Their safety and wellbeing was a priority concern above everything. Along with regular education through entertainment activities, Total 10799 youth and adolescents were connected with Pathshala in the reporting period.
The project has been ended with good results. An evaluation was conducted in the 5th year of the project. According to the evaluation the project is on track.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
